model: Schneider Electric PowerLogic CM4000 via BASgatewayLX
applies_to: Schneider Electric (Square D) PowerLogic CM4000-series circuit monitors on Modbus, read by a BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile for the PowerLogic CM4000: 711 objects (664 AI, 47 BI), 68 polled by default (the 1-second current, voltage, unbalance, power, PF and frequency values). 100 ms readings, min/max, demand, energy registers, THD and status bits are unpolled.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile Power_Logic_CM4000_Power_Meter_b_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the maker's Modbus register document (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/PowerLogicCM4000.pdf).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 68 of the 711 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.
Some names appear more than once in the profile as published (Installed Log Memory); they are kept as printed and told apart by instance.
Energy values are split over four registers each (Reg 1-4) as in the CM4000 map; combine them per the register document.

integration.summary: Map real power total (1 s), voltage L-L average (1 s) and current 3-phase average (1 s) first. The listed objects are read-only.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
